title: Biodegradable Cellulose-Based Hybrid Hydrogels for Rainfed Agriculture: Impact of Crosslinker Type on Pore Structure and Thermal Stability
content: Biodegradable sodium carboxymethylcellulose-hydrolyzed polyacrylonitrile-acrylic acid (CMC-GIPAN-AA) ternary hybrid hydrogels were synthesized via free-radical graft copolymerization to mitigate drought stress in rainfed agriculture. To evaluate crosslinking eﬀects on network architecture and performance, rigid covalent agents (epichlorohydrin, EXG; N,N'-methylenebisacrylamide, MBAA) and a dynamic amine-functionalized agent (urotropine, UR) were systematically compared. Multi-instrumental analysis revealed that covalent crosslinking generated dense, thick-walled mesoporous networks with restricted surface areas (BET = 7.24 m²/g for EXG). Conversely, urotropine integration established ﬂexible ionic/coordination complexes, yielding a highly porous, thin-walled macroporous morphology with targeted nitrogen integration (3.46 wt%) and high sodium content (21.96 wt%). Consequently, the urotropine-crosslinked hydrogel (N2) achieved an exceptional equilibrium swelling capacity (Qeq) of 680 g/g in DI water, representing a 2.19-fold and 2.83-fold increase over EXG (310 g/g) and MBAA (240 g/g), respectively. Kinetic modeling conﬁrmed anomalous non-Fickian diﬀusion (n = 0.68) for N2, driven by rapid chain relaxation. TGA/DTA demonstrated enhanced initial moisture retention (28.6%) and gradual multi-stage thermal degradation. In 30-day soil drying tests at 30 °C, 0.5 wt% N2-amended soil retained 31.8% moisture content, whereas unamended soil completely desiccated (0.0%) within 25 days. Thus, urotropine-driven dynamic crosslinking provides a superior molecular design for engineering high-performance soil conditioners.
